title: Fluorescent Painting 3.0
content: Fluorescence microscopy is a powerful tool for localizing specific molecules within a sample. However, the weak and often transient signal given off by many fluorochromes presents challenges to its implementation. Nonetheless, the ability to manipulate a fluorescent signal has been key to the development of “super-­resolution” techniques that provide microscopic resolution below the diffraction limit imposed by direct imaging techniques. Current “super-resolution” microscopy techniques improve resolution by either reducing the point spread function of a fluorescent molecule’s signal or by separating the signal of a single molecule from that of closely adjacent molecules.
